exposure: Gestational age at birth (very preterm: 28-31 weeks, moderately preterm: 32-33 weeks, late preterm: 34-36 weeks, early term: 37-38 weeks, full term: >=39 weeks)
outcome: Individual cognitive domain scores (vocabulary, working memory, episodic memory, short-delay recall, long-delay recall)
cohort: A cohort of 5946 children aged 9 to 10 years participating in the prospective, multicenter Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development Study.
finding: Moderately preterm birth (32-33 weeks) was associated with lower composite cognitive scores and deficits in specific cognitive domains in children aged 9-10 years, independent of socioeconomic status, genetics, and other risk factors, with the lowest cognitive scores observed in those born at 32 weeks or less.
gest_age: Very preterm (28-31 weeks), moderately preterm (32-33 weeks), late preterm (34-36 weeks), early term (37-38 weeks), and full term (>=39 weeks)
